setTips.starter: 60 hand-picked words that trip up spelling-to-sound rules: irregular words, loans, rare long words, names and dialect words
setTips.random1000: 1,000 random words from the pronunciation dictionary: 400 common, 300 mid-frequency, 300 rare. Truth is the dictionary entry
setTips.heteronyms: 32 meanings of 16 words with two pronunciations. The task is to pick the pronunciation that goes with the meaning
setTips.bank: Every word in the word bank that has a dictionary pronunciation. The truth is the CMU entry, so a miss can be the dictionary's error or a second valid pronunciation. Only wrong answers and a spread of right ones are kept for browsing.

lookup.name: Dictionary lookup
lookup.blurb: Read the word in the pronunciation dictionary. The reference answer.
steps: Look the word up in CMU.
Take the first listed pronunciation.
lookup.example: colonel → K ER N AH L

wikipron.name: Second dictionary
wikipron.blurb: Look the word up in WikiPron, a different dictionary built from Wiktionary.
steps: Look the word up in WikiPron US.
Convert its symbols to ours.
Take the first pronunciation.
wikipron.example: A second source for words the first one lacks

checked.name: Generate, then check
checked.blurb: eSpeak writes a pronunciation. If the second dictionary agrees, accept it. If not, flag it.
steps: eSpeak generates a pronunciation from the spelling.
Look the word up in WikiPron.
Agree: accept. Disagree or missing: flag for a person.
No model call is needed to tell which answers to trust.

espeak.name: Rule-based generator
espeak.blurb: eSpeak turns spelling into sounds with rules and a long exceptions list. Free and fast.
steps: Send the word to eSpeak with the US voice.
Convert its IPA output to our symbols.
espeak.example: island → AY L AH N D

unit.name: Unit statistics
unit.blurb: Build a pronunciation from how our 126,000 aligned words pair spellings with sounds.
steps: Split the word into letter groups.
Give each group its most common sounds from our aligned words, leaving the word itself out.
Keep the highest-scoring whole pronunciation.
unit.example: cat → K AH T (context-blind, so weak)

pool-jev-ipa.name: Candidates + Jev, IPA
pool-jev-ipa.blurb: Collect candidate pronunciations from eSpeak and unit statistics, show them in IPA, and ask Jev to pick.
steps: Gather up to 6 distinct candidates.
Write each in IPA.
One question per word, asked twice with shuffled order, averaged.
pool-jev-ipa.example: Which is the correct standard American pronunciation of 'colonel'?

pool-jev-ipa-rhyme.name: Candidates + Jev, IPA and rhyme word
pool-jev-ipa-rhyme.blurb: Same, with a word the candidate ends like, so Jev has a sound to compare.
steps: Same candidates, written in IPA.
Each also says which common word it ends like.
Jev picks.

pool-jev.name: Candidates + Jev, respelling
pool-jev.blurb: Same candidates, written as plain-English respellings with a rhyme word.
steps: Candidates written like k-er-n-uh-l.
Each says which common word it ends like.
Jev picks.

pool-jev-plain.name: Candidates + Jev, respelling only
steps: Candidates written like k-er-n-uh-l.
Jev picks.

pool-llama.name: Candidates + local Llama
pool-llama.blurb: The same pick, by Llama 3.2 3B on this computer. No API.
steps: Same candidates as the Jev versions.
Llama answers with a letter, twice with shuffled order.
